Good luck to anyone who wants to watch a film that seeks to evoke sympathy for Donald Trump. It's bad enough seeing videos of him in real life by accident, I can't imagine ever being compelled to watch a dramatisation of his early years.

Guess we should only make movies about good people, huh? I thoroughly enjoyed the film, although I hold the highest disregard for Trump as a (public) person. A very interesting individual he is, though
What are you talking about?
He's the most important American of the early 21th century, I think it's good to learn how he became the person he is.

You’ve sold me on the worth of this film, but I still won’t be watching it - not yet, anyway.   
I remember when Paul Greengrass’s film United 93 came out (in 2006) during the trailer someone in the audience shouted “too soon.” This is how I feel about The Apprentice; we’re too busy trying to deal with this monster in our lives to appreciate a subtle period piece on it.
Absolutely agree. And the film isn’t trying to glorify him or in any way justify his methods, nor trying to evoke sympathy for the person. It simply puts his story in context.

I agree, but at the same time... Trump news is inescapable right now. The hateful rhetoric and threats he spews on a daily basis is exhausting.  I have no doubt this is a great movie, and yeah, he's an interesting individual, but the idea of watching this right now is the opposite of appealing.
Biopics are probably the worst way to learn about a person, tho. They capture vibes, not reality.
Fair enough but it's only about 10 years of his life.

People are willing to watch Vice, Napoleon, etc. but not this? I don't get it

This comment is in very poor taste. While I understand the (presumably honest) intention of it, but let’s not suggest that a trashy-on-purpose, in no way subtle black comedy about the origins of Donald Trump is depicting events that are in any way comparable to the unfathomably horrific ones depicted in United 93.
My apologies. I didn’t mean to draw parallels between the two events.

I’m talking about all the films I’ve sat through trailers for the past 24 years while waiting to see the few films good enough to pay $15 to see in the theater. I’m talking about the general quality of mass-market films declining after 1999. I’m talking about the multiplexes being taken over by grown men in tights.

The movie kind of tries to force you to sympathize with him, and it does it badly. The writing is not very adventurous, most scenes are structured in a very approachable and familiar way. Since most movies have sympathetic protagonists, the script kind of doesn’t realize how much it’s forcing you into his perspective without criticizing it or maintaining a distance that allows you to judge it slightly more objectively.

The way to do this isn’t to swerve back and forth between hand holding the audience through his personal failings and make him sympathetic, it’s portray this guy as objectively as possible

I couldn’t have said it better. I’m amazed that I saw a movie that made me feel sympathy for Donald Trump and Roy Cohn (though never both at the same time), but hey, good art will do that kinda thing.

Don't worry, you didn't. Any sane person understands the comparison you are trying to make and in fact I feel the same way about The Apprentice. I know it's good, but I still don't have an inkling to watch it.

Just a small bit of tangential writing advicwe but you shouldn't start your concluding paragraph with "In conclusion". We know it's a conclusion because it's the last paragraph. And you summarise your points.
Okay, thank you.

A friend of mine worked on the VFX for this film. One of the jobs was to tidy up the joins on the prosthetics, which tended to become unattached at the end of each days shoot. I think the temperatures in New York contributed to the issue. In terms of digital compositing, I don't know whether they matched Kodak film stock from the 1980's or the NTSC television standard.

I also understand the comparison, and understand the (valid) fear behind it, and am not surprised by the downvotes my reply received as this is evidently a forum which skews Left. But let’s be clear: a film depicting 40 people - and an unborn child - being murdered by Al-Qaeda in the most horrific circumstances imaginable, using a grimly sickening vérité style, is objectively *not* the same as a black-comedy about Donald Trump’s early years - and one portraying him as the power-hungry yet hapless beast he is at that! - which apparently 90% of this thread haven’t even watched despite commenting.

Let’s not pretend these films are the same, and let’s not pretend the circumstances they depict are remotely comparable. Too soon? Maybe. Close to home? For US audiences, definitely - and as it should be. I for one think it’s amazing they’ve managed to even get this out before the election, though props for suggesting that thinking the above makes me in some way mentally ill.
A comparison does not need to be a one to one equal to understand what someone is saying. No one is minimizing anything, but you are making a mountain out of a like hole.

Deleted my comment because it got a lot of downvotes. Shame we can't discuss this/argue about it calmly without being made to feel wrong before I even read the replies. Thought this sub would be totally different in that regard.

Your comment felt more reactive than thoughtful, criticizing the movie and those who wanted to watch it without having seen it yourself. It came off as dismissive without any real basis. Hardly an invitation for “calm discussion” from your end. That being said, I agree with the sub not being what it used to be. But comments like yours is one of the reasons for that, not the response

That's fair enough, but you did jump to the conclusion that what I meant was that we should "only make films about good people", which is obviously absurd. My comment was in direct reference to the first sentence of OPs post. Anyway, maybe when Trump is long gone they will make films about how interesting a character he was, but unless it's a hit job seeking to show how disgusting this very current person is/was, I don't really see why this has been made now. Unless, of course, to "evoke sympathy" for the man. Which is something I have zero interest in. (I was very interested in this movie when I first heard about it!)
You are an unbelievably corny dork
